sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Against the advice of public health officials and the wishes of its own governor,
sentences.zh: 不顾公共卫生官员的建议和其自身州长的意愿，

sentences.en: Wisconsin will hold its Democratic primary today in the middle of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州今天将在大流行期间举行民主党初选。

sentences.en: A Stead Herndon on how that happened.
sentences.zh: 阿斯蒂德·赫恩顿将带我们了解这是如何发生的。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, April 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月7日，星期二。

sentences.en: March was always going to be one of the most consequential months of the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 三月原本注定是总统大选中最具影响力的月份之一。

sentences.en: By the time we get to the middle of March, though.
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们进入三月中旬时。

sentences.en: So here's what we're watching.
sentences.zh: 以下是我们正在关注的内容。

sentences.en: Breaking news.
sentences.zh: 突发新闻。

sentences.en: Louisiana officially could become the first state to postpone its Democratic primary election over the coronavirus pandemic.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州正式成为第一个因冠状病毒大流行而推迟民主党初选的州。

sentences.en: It becomes clear that the coronavirus global health pandemic has really upended the race completely.
sentences.zh: 显然，冠状病毒全球健康大流行彻底颠覆了这场竞选。

sentences.en: After Super Tuesday, states that are scheduled to vote start postponing and sometimes our canceling their scheduled primaries.
sentences.zh: “超级星期二”之后，原定于投票的各州开始推迟，有时甚至取消原定的初选。

sentences.en: Georgia becoming the second state to delay its presidential primary.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州成为第二个推迟总统初选的州。

sentences.en: Kentucky announced that they'd delay their contest as well.
sentences.zh: 肯塔基州也宣布将推迟其初选。

sentences.en: Ohio's governor pushed back its primary just hours before polls were set to open.
sentences.zh: 就在投票站开放前几小时，俄亥俄州州长推迟了初选。

sentences.en: Other states, Connecticut, Indiana, and Maryland.
sentences.zh: 其他州还有康涅狄格州、印第安纳州和马里兰州。

sentences.en: These are all states that said that the public health crisis was too great for them to hold in-person elections in March.
sentences.zh: 这些州都表示，公共卫生危机过于严重，无法在三月份举行面对面的选举。

sentences.en: But there's one state that refuses to budge, even as public health officials are urging them.
sentences.zh: 但有一个州拒绝妥协，尽管公共卫生官员极力敦促他们这样做。

sentences.en: And states across the country have taken that drastic step.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的州都采取了这一激进的步骤。

sentences.en: It's Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 这就是威斯康星州。

sentences.en: And what explains that?
sentences.zh: 这该如何解释呢？

sentences.en: What's happening in Wisconsin?
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, when most people look at these presidential primaries, particularly in a state like Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 当大多数人审视这些总统初选时，特别是在威斯康星州这样的地方，

sentences.en: they think that this is just about the two candidates at the top, Joe Biden versus Bernie Sanders and who gets the delegates out of that.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这只是关于顶部的两位候选人，乔·拜登对阵伯尼·桑德斯，以及谁能从中获得代表权。

sentences.en: But the reason why Wisconsin was holding out and keeping its primary schedule was really to do with more state and local concerns.
sentences.zh: 但威斯康星州之所以坚持并保留其初选日程，实际上更多是出于对州和地方事务的考量。

sentences.en: Initially, the Democratic governor, Tony Evers, and state Republican leaders were on the same page.
sentences.zh: 最初，民主党州长托尼·埃弗斯和州共和党领袖意见一致。

sentences.en: They both agreed that the April 7th election should go forward.
sentences.zh: 他们都同意4月7日的选举应该继续进行。

sentences.en: And they said so for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 他们提出这一主张有几个原因。

sentences.en: Not only had the virus not really ravaged the state in the same way that we have seen in other parts of the country at the initial time in March when they were making this decision,
sentences.zh: 不仅在三月份他们做出这一决定的初期，病毒尚未像我们在该国其他地方看到的那样严重肆虐该州，

sentences.en: but they agreed on the importance of the state and local races that would be decided down ballot on the same day of the presidential primary.
sentences.zh: 而且他们一致认为，在总统初选同日决出的州和地方竞选同样至关重要。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure people understand the complexity of our spring general election.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保人们理解我们春季大选的复杂性。

sentences.en: Races like sheriffs and mayors and court judges, there's a particularly important Supreme Court race that's happening in the state.
sentences.zh: 诸如治安官、市长和法官之类的竞选，特别是该州正在举行一场极其重要的最高法院竞选。

sentences.en: And both sides agreed that filling these roles was important for the continuance of state government.
sentences.zh: 双方都认为，填补这些职位对于州政府的持续运转至关重要。

sentences.en: How long do we potentially leave offices not filled because we're into July or August and we haven't held a general election?
sentences.zh: 如果我们拖到七月或八月还没有举行大选，这些职位我们要空置多久？

sentences.en: And that's why they proceeded with the primary.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们继续推进初选的原因。

sentences.en: You know, I want to give credit to Governor Evers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我要赞赏埃弗斯州长。

sentences.en: I agree with his decision to say that we are going to hold this election.
sentences.zh: 我同意他关于我们将举行这次选举的决定。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So despite the risks of holding an in-person primary in the middle of a pandemic, despite the fact that many states are postponing these primaries,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管在大流行期间举行面对面初选存在风险，尽管许多州都在推迟这些初选，

sentences.en: the Republican and Democratic officials in Wisconsin say that this is necessary for the functioning of their government.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州的共和党和民主党官员表示，这对于他们政府的运作是必不可少的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's the position they held for about a week.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们维持了大约一周的立场。

sentences.en: And what happens after a week?
sentences.zh: 一周后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, kind of most clearly, the factors around the decision change.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最明显的是，围绕这一决定的因素改变了。

sentences.en: We need an all-hands-on-deck approach to stop the spread of COVID-19 in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 我们需要采取全民动员的方法来阻止新冠病毒在威斯康星州的传播。

sentences.en: The pandemic becomes more acutely felt in the Midwest and particularly in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 大流行在中西部地区，尤其是在威斯康星州，变得更加深重。

sentences.en: But here is the bottom line.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的一点是。

sentences.en: Folks need to start taking this seriously.
sentences.zh: 人们需要开始认真对待这件事了。

sentences.en: So today I'm asking for your help.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我请求你们的帮助。

sentences.en: And the governor issues a stay-at-home order, like many other governors did across the country, and closes all non-essential businesses.
sentences.zh: 州长发布了居家令，就像全国许多其他州长一样，并关闭了所有非必要企业。

sentences.en: It's not something I wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 这不是我想做的事。

sentences.en: And it's not something I take lightly.
sentences.zh: 也不是一件我轻率对待的事。

sentences.en: And people across the state are starting to say, well, if we can't leave our houses, how are we supposed to vote?
sentences.zh: 全州的人们开始说，如果我们不能离开家，我们又该如何投票呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And what's the answer?
sentences.zh: 答案是什么？

sentences.en: The governor and state Republicans keep holding this line, that voting was something that was so essential, that the primary was something that was so important,
sentences.zh: 州长和州共和党人依然坚持这一立场，即投票是如此基本的事情，初选是如此重要，

sentences.en: that they would try to find some workarounds.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们会尝试寻找一些变通办法。

sentences.en: That included expanding access to absentee ballots and encouraging people to use that measure.
sentences.zh: 这包括扩大缺席选票的获取途径，并鼓励人们使用这种方式。

sentences.en: It included counties taking precautionary measures, which include maybe drive-thru voting or socially distanced lines.
sentences.zh: 这包括各县采取预防措施，可能包括得来速投票或保持社交距离的排队方式。

sentences.en: But besides all of these creative measures, there is an increasing fear, particularly among poll workers, that the election would be unsafe for them to staff.
sentences.zh: 但除了所有这些创新的举措之外，人们越来越担忧，尤其是投票站工作人员，这次选举对他们来说是不安全的。

sentences.en: These are people who, 90% of them, are senior citizens.
sentences.zh: 这些人中，有90%是老年人。

sentences.en: Poll workers.
sentences.zh: 投票站工作人员。

sentences.en: One of the most vulnerable population to this deadly virus.
sentences.zh: 这是面对这种致命病毒最脆弱的人群之一。

sentences.en: And they start dropping off, informing their local jurisdictions that they don't think that they want to participate in the scheduled election.
sentences.zh: 他们开始退出，通知当地管辖区他们认为自己不想参加预定的选举。

sentences.en: A survey from the Election Commission in the state showed that more than 100 jurisdictions cannot adequately staff their polling locations because they wouldn't have the right poll workers to do so.
sentences.zh: 该州选举委员会的一项调查显示，超过100个司法管辖区无法为其投票点配备足够的工作人员，因为他们没有合适的工作人员来完成这项工作。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That becomes the first real point of pressure to say, how can this election go forward?
sentences.zh: 这成为第一个真正的施压点，让人质疑这次选举怎么能继续进行？

sentences.en: So what do officials do in response to this severe shortage of poll workers?
sentences.zh: 面对如此严重的工作人员短缺，官员们作何反应？

sentences.en: Well, they go back to trying to find creative workarounds.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们重新开始寻找创新的变通办法。

sentences.en: So the first thing that some of the local jurisdictions do is close and limit their polling locations.
sentences.zh: 因此，一些地方管辖区采取的第一件事就是关闭和限制他们的投票点。

sentences.en: Some of the more drastic examples include Milwaukee, the biggest city in the state, going from 180 polling locations typically down to just five or seven.
sentences.zh: 一些比较极端的例子包括密尔沃基，该州最大的城市，通常有180个投票点，现在缩减到只有5到7个。

sentences.en: And yet everyone still seems committed to holding this election.
sentences.zh: 然而每个人似乎仍然致力于举行这次选举。

sentences.en: They were.
sentences.zh: 他们确实如此。

sentences.en: Until the virus intensifies in the state and cases increase, as the deaths increase, that's when you see a real shift from the governor.
sentences.zh: 直到病毒在该州加剧、病例增加、死亡人数上升，你才会看到州长的真正转变。

sentences.en: Hi there, folks.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Governor Evers here.
sentences.zh: 我是埃弗斯州长。

sentences.en: And it's a big one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大举措。

sentences.en: So today I'm asking the legislature to come together to take bipartisan action to ensure that every registered voter receives an absentee ballot to vote in the upcoming election.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天我要求立法机关团结起来，采取两党合作的行动，确保每一位注册选民都收到一张缺席选票，以便在即将到来的选举中投票。

sentences.en: He proposes a dramatic expansion in the state's absentee ballot voting system, essentially making it a universal vote-by-mail system.
sentences.zh: 他提议大幅扩大该州的缺席选票投票系统，实质上使其成为全民邮寄投票系统。

sentences.en: So I hope that the legislature will act swiftly to send absentee ballots to every single registered voter living in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望立法机关迅速行动，将缺席选票寄给威斯康星州的每一位注册选民。

sentences.en: The state would mail 3.3 million eligible voters a ballot, whether they requested it or not.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是否要求，该州都会向330万符合条件的选民邮寄一张选票。

sentences.en: And that represents a real change in how kind of the electoral process would work throughout the state.
sentences.zh: 这代表了全州选举过程运作方式的真正改变。

sentences.en: This is not a Republican issue or a Democratic issue.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个共和党的问题，也不是一个民主党的问题。

sentences.en: This is an issue of democracy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个民主的问题。

sentences.en: I don't care who gets the credit.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎谁来邀功。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure that everyone has a chance to cast their ballot this April.
sentences.zh: 我只想确保每个人都有机会在今年四月投出选票。

sentences.en: Thanks for watching and let's get it done, folks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢观看，让我们把它办成，伙计们。

sentences.en: And that's when we really see the partisan pushback start.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，我们真正看到了党派的强烈反对开始出现。

sentences.en: What began as a Democratic governor and a Republican state legislature that were basically on the same page has now devolved into what is by all accounts a partisan bloodbath.
sentences.zh: 原本意见基本一致的民主党州长和共和党州议会，现在演变成了一场名副其实的党派血洗。

sentences.en: From the moment that Evers proposes that every person would be mailed a ballot, whether they asked for it or not, Republicans go haywire.
sentences.zh: 从埃弗斯提议无论人们是否索要都向每个人邮寄选票的那一刻起，共和党人就彻底疯狂了。

sentences.en: Right now, Senate Majority Leader Scott Fitzgerald is calling this idea a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 目前，参议院多数党领袖斯科特·菲茨杰拉德称这一想法为幻想。

sentences.en: Yeah, this has probably been my biggest disappointment so far in working with the administration since this all happened.
sentences.zh: 是的，自这一切发生以来，这可能是我在与政府合作中最大的失望。

sentences.en: They say that this is not only logistically and practical.
sentences.zh: 他们说这不仅在后勤上不切实际。

sentences.en: It was completely disingenuous for the governor to tape a video and post it as if this was reality, to float the idea that they were going to find enough outer envelopes,
sentences.zh: 州长录制视频并发布，假装这一切都是现实，抛出他们将找到足够的外部信封、选票本身、带有一流邮资的内部信封并将其邮寄给威斯康星州330万人的想法，完全是凭空捏造的。

sentences.en: balance themselves, inner envelopes with first class postage and mail it out to 3.3 million people in Wisconsin is completely made up.
sentences.zh: 完全是凭空捏造的。

sentences.en: But also kind of morally and democratically wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且在道德和民主上也是错误的。

sentences.en: You know, that happens sometimes, I guess, if you're feeling pressure from one of your own special interests or from the party themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想如果你面临来自某个特殊利益集团或政党本身的压力，有时就会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: And Evers knows that state law does not allow him to kind of unilaterally make huge changes in how Wisconsin runs the election.
sentences.zh: 埃弗斯知道，州法律不允许他单方面对威斯康星州选举的运作方式做出巨大改变。

sentences.en: Folks, I can't move this election or change the rules on my own.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，我不能凭一己之力推动这次选举或改变规则。

sentences.en: My hands are tied.
sentences.zh: 我的手被绑住了。

sentences.en: He needs the help of the legislature.
sentences.zh: 他需要立法机关的帮助。

sentences.en: And so one of the measures he tries to do is call a special session of the legislature and encourage them to delay the election and implement changes that would allow every person to be able to vote without going in person.
sentences.zh: 因此他尝试采取的措施之一是召集立法机关举行特别会议，鼓励他们推迟选举并实施变革，使每个人都能在不用亲自前往的情况下投票。

sentences.en: I urge legislators to take this call for a special session seriously.
sentences.zh: 我敦促立法委员认真对待这次召开特别会议的呼吁。

sentences.en: It doesn't go well.
sentences.zh: 进展并不顺利。

sentences.en: The legislature gavels in a session this past Saturday.
sentences.zh: 立法机关在上周六敲击法槌召开了会议。

sentences.en: The April 2020 special session of the Senate will come to order.
sentences.zh: 2020年4月参议院特别会议现在开始。

sentences.en: Without objection, the April 2020 special session will stand adjourned until Monday, April 6.
sentences.zh: 如果没有异议，2020年4月特别会议将休会至4月6日星期一。

sentences.en: And less than a minute later.
sentences.zh: 不到一分钟后。

sentences.en: The April 2020 special session is adjourned.
sentences.zh: 2020年4月特别会议休会。

sentences.en: Gavels out.
sentences.zh: 敲槌宣布散会。

sentences.en: This is kind of an extraordinary move by the legislature to really thumb their nose at the power of the executive and the governor.
sentences.zh: 这是立法机关采取的一种非同寻常的举动，公然蔑视行政长官和州长的权力。

sentences.en: The biggest elected official in the state has called them into session and said, take up this issue.
sentences.zh: 州内最大的民选官员召集他们开会并说，处理这个议题吧。

sentences.en: And they basically start the session and end it without doing what he asked.
sentences.zh: 而他们基本上是刚开始开会就结束了，并没有做他要求的事。

sentences.en: So the Republicans do not grant the governor his wish for a mail-in balloting system.
sentences.zh: 因此，共和党人没有满足州长对邮寄投票系统的愿望。

sentences.en: I said,
sentences.zh: 我说，

sentences.en: why is it that Wisconsin has so quickly erupted into a really nasty partisan battle over something as seemingly basic as making sure people can vote safely in a primary election?
sentences.zh: 为什么威斯康星州会如此迅速地爆发一场真正恶劣的党派争斗，而争斗的起因仅仅是确保人们在初选中安全投票这样看似基础的事情？

sentences.en: I mean, that would seem to be in everyone's bipartisan interest to protect life, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，保护生命似乎符合每个人的两党利益，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Democrats and Republicans will be casting ballots.
sentences.zh: 民主党人和共和党人都将投出选票。

sentences.en: It would seem as if safe voting and public health would be an issue in which partisanship would be left to the side and that Democrats and Republicans can agree on the best way to move forward.
sentences.zh: 似乎安全投票和公共卫生本应是一个可以抛开党派之争、让民主党和共和党就前进的最佳方式达成一致的问题。

sentences.en: But in Wisconsin, there is no issue in which that can be left to side.
sentences.zh: 但在威斯康星州，没有任何问题是可以抛开党派之争的。

sentences.en: What we see is a state that has become so deeply rested by Republican control that even something like safe voting turns into a mud feSt.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是一个饱受共和党控制摧残的州，以至于连安全投票这样的小事都变成了泥潭之争。

sentences.en: And for this governor, for the Democratic governor, Tony Evers, that's been clear since the day he was elected.
sentences.zh: 对这位州长，对于民主党州长托尼·埃弗斯来说，自从他当选那一天起，这一点就很清楚了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: As I said, where does this political dysfunction that you're describing in Wisconsin, where does that start?
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，你所描述的威斯康星州的这种政治功能失调，它是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: Well, the state is one that is unique in its political history.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个州在政治历史上是独一无二的。

sentences.en: Few places reflect the growing political chasm in the U.S., as does the state of Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 很少有地方能像威斯康星州这样，反映出美国日益扩大的政治鸿沟。

sentences.en: Wisconsin was a united Republican government under Scott Walker.
sentences.zh: 在斯科特·沃克执政期间，威斯康星州是一个由共和党全面执政的政府。

sentences.en: Republicans won everything in Wisconsin in 2010.
sentences.zh: 2010年，共和党人在威斯康星州赢得了所有选举。

sentences.en: From 2010 until 2018.
They won the legislature.
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了议会。

sentences.en: They won this Republican majority in the Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 他们在威斯康星州赢得了这个共和党多数地位。

sentences.en: And this wasn't just a Republican government that passed kind of conventional conservative bills.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一个通过了常规保守派法案的共和党政府。

sentences.en: This was seen as really a laboratory of conservative ideas.
sentences.zh: 这里曾被视为保守派思想的真正实验室。

sentences.en: Governor Scott Walker is the man at the center of a bitter fight that has cleaved Wisconsin like a block of its best cheddar cheese.
sentences.zh: 州长斯科特·沃克是这场激烈争斗的核心人物，这场争斗把威斯康星州撕裂得就像一块上好的切达干酪。

sentences.en: And so we saw a government that targeted teachers unions, that seized power on keyboards,
sentences.zh: 因此我们看到一个将矛头对准教师工会的政府，一个通过键盘夺取权力的政府，

sentences.en: and really kind of had a wish list of conservative ideas nationally playing out in the state.
sentences.zh: 并且实际上在州内上演了一种全国性的保守派思想愿望清单。

sentences.en: He proposed slashing spending, raising no taxes, and most controversial of all, sharply curtailing public employees' right to collective bargaining.
sentences.zh: 他提议大幅削减开支，不加税，而最具争议的是，大幅限制公共雇员的集体谈判权。

sentences.en: Even as the state voted for Barack Obama twice.
sentences.zh: 尽管该州曾两次投票支持巴拉克·奥巴马。

sentences.en: Republican Governor Scott Walker has won his re-election bid.
sentences.zh: 共和党州长斯科特·沃克赢得了连任竞选。

sentences.en: They kept winning.
sentences.zh: 他们不断获胜。

sentences.en: For the third time in four years, Republican Scott Walker has won a statewide election for governor.
sentences.zh: 在四年内的第三次选举中，共和党人斯科特·沃克赢得了全州州长选举。

sentences.en: So by the time you get to 2018.
sentences.zh: 所以到了2018年的时候。

sentences.en: Major shift happened overnight.
sentences.zh: 重大转变在一夜之间发生。

sentences.en: Wisconsin voters, you've elected a Democrat as governor.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州的选民们，你们选出了一位民主党人担任州长。

sentences.en: When Walker loses his re-election bid to Tony Evers.
sentences.zh: 当时沃克在连任竞选中输给了托尼·埃弗斯。

sentences.en: The race was almost too close to call.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选结果几乎难分伯仲。

sentences.en: But overnight, Democrat Tony Evers narrowly beat out GOP incumbent Scott Walker, denying him a third term.
sentences.zh: 但一夜之间，民主党人托尼·埃弗斯险胜共和党现任州长斯科特·沃克，打破了后者三连任的希望。

sentences.en: Republicans in the state legislature have already learned a lesson from the years prior.
sentences.zh: 州议会中的共和党人已经从前几年的经历中吸取了教训。

sentences.en: That it's more important to wield power than it is to be seen as a political compromiser.
sentences.zh: 那就是掌握权力比被视为政治妥协者更为重要。

sentences.en: So how does that play out when all of a sudden there is a Democratic governor in Evers who I assume wants to start making compromises with the Republican legislature?
sentences.zh: 那么，当埃弗斯这位我猜想希望开始与共和党议会达成妥协的民主党州长突然上台时，局面会如何发展？

sentences.en: The Republicans make clear that that is not what they're interested in.
sentences.zh: 共和党人明确表示这并不是他们感兴趣的。

sentences.en: Republicans, stung by their losses in the midterms, are moving forward with last-ditch efforts to hang on to power.
sentences.zh: 受到中期选举失利打击的共和党人，正推进最后的努力以死守权力。

sentences.en: It's happening in at least two swing states, Wisconsin and Michigan.
sentences.zh: 这种情况至少发生在两个摇摆州：威斯康星州和密歇根州。

sentences.en: The country is really watching this morning as lawmakers here in Wisconsin work through the night to amend and vote on a number of bills.
sentences.zh: 今天早上全国都在密切关注，因为威斯康星州的议员们通宵达旦地对多项法案进行修正和投票。

sentences.en: So in a special session that happens before Evers takes office, Republicans do a kind of classic power grab.
sentences.zh: 因此，在埃弗斯就职之前召开的特别会议上，共和党人进行了某种典型的夺权。

sentences.en: Wisconsin's Republican-controlled legislature passed a series of bills late Wednesday night that would limit the powers of incoming Democratic governor Tony Evers.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州由共和党控制的议会周三深夜通过了一系列法案，将限制新任民主党州长托尼·埃弗斯的权力。

sentences.en: They pass a number of bills that limit the power of the incoming Democratic governor and take away things that were available to his Republican predecessor.
sentences.zh: 他们通过了一系列法案，限制新任民主党州长的权力，并剥夺了其共和党前任所拥有的权力。

sentences.en: Now the bills would put lawmakers in charge of litigation which would effectively block incoming Democratic governor Tony Evers and the Democratic attorney general-elect from withdrawing the state from a lawsuit to overturn Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 这些法案将使议员负责诉讼事务，从而有效地阻止即将上任的民主党州长托尼·埃弗斯和候任民主党总检察长撤回该州旨在推翻奥巴马医改的诉讼。

sentences.en: So Evers would not have the power to make key appointments.
sentences.zh: 因此埃弗斯将没有权力进行关键任命。

sentences.en: And another bill would require the governor to get permission from the legislature to ban guns.
sentences.zh: 另一项法案则要求州长在禁止枪支时必须获得议会的批准。

sentences.en: Evers would not have the power to regulate guns in the same way that it existed for his predecessor.
sentences.zh: 埃弗斯将无法像其前任那样以相同的方式监管枪支。

sentences.en: They also limit early voting, which is a kind of tool of access to the ballot box that has sometimes helped Democrats because more people in bigger areas can get to the polls.
sentences.zh: 他们还限制了提前投票，这是一种有时对民主党有利的选民参与渠道，因为较大地区的更多人能够前往投票站。

sentences.en: These were all really nakedly partisan.
sentences.zh: 这些都实在是赤裸裸的党派偏见。

sentences.en: And Republicans didn't really even try to hide it.
sentences.zh: 而且共和党人甚至没有试图掩饰这一点。

sentences.en: We don't want to usurp his power.
sentences.zh: 我们并不想篡夺他的权力。

sentences.en: That's never been our goal.
sentences.zh: 这从来都不是我们的目标。

sentences.en: Our goal is just to guarantee that we have an opportunity to sit at the table, negotiate, and do it fairly.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标只是确保我们有机会坐在谈判桌前进行谈判，并且做到公平。

sentences.en: It puts us on an equal playing field as the legislature.
sentences.zh: 这让我们与议会处于平等的竞技场上。

sentences.en: And I think that's a positive step for the state of Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对威斯康星州来说是积极的一步。

sentences.en: So that is the political backdrop, you're saying, for this current battle over how to hold a primary in the middle of a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，这就是当前这场关于如何在疫情期间举行初选的争斗的政治背景。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is that sense of affirmation, the sense of rightness that Republicans enter in to Evers' administration with.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是这种笃定感，这种共和党人带着正当性进入埃弗斯政府的心态。

sentences.en: And it allows them to openly flout the typical means of political pressure that the governor tries to put on them around the election.
sentences.zh: 这让他们能够公开无视州长试图在选举前后向他们施加的典型政治压力手段。

sentences.en: The legislature, they came in, they gaveled in for about 10 seconds, gaveled out, and they moved on.
sentences.zh: 议会来到现场，开会大约十秒钟就宣布休会，然后接着干别的去了。

sentences.en: They said that was not a serious proposal and said the time for proposals like that was several weeks ago when the crisis began.
sentences.zh: 他们称这不是一个认真的提议，并表示提出这种提议的时间是在危机开始的几周前。

sentences.en: So what happens after that special session, that minute-long special session about the election?
sentences.zh: 那么在那次特别会议之后发生了什么，那场关于选举的持续了一分钟的特别会议？

sentences.en: Well, there's been a significant amount of legal legislation that has surrounded all of this political action.
sentences.zh: 嗯，围绕所有这些政治行动，已经出现了大量的法律诉讼。

sentences.en: So much going on here at the state capitol today.
sentences.zh: 今天州议会大厦这里有太多事情在发生。

sentences.en: Let's break down and give you a brief summary of what happened today, because it's been a wild day politically.
sentences.zh: 让我们来剖析并简要总结今天发生的事情，因为这在政治上是疯狂的一天。

sentences.en: There was a court ruling that basically affirmed that the Republicans probably have control over when the election should be held.
sentences.zh: 有一项法院裁决基本上确认了共和党人可能对选举应在何时举行拥有控制权。

sentences.en: But the ruling expanded access to absentee voting.
sentences.zh: 但该裁决扩大了缺席投票的渠道。

sentences.en: Republicans appealed that straight to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 共和党人直接向美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院提起了上诉。

sentences.en: And then on Monday...
sentences.zh: 然后在周一……

sentences.en: It started with Governor Evers issuing an executive order pushing back the spring election from tomorrow to June 9th.
sentences.zh: 一切始于埃弗斯州长发布行政命令，将春季初选从明天推迟到6月9日。

sentences.en: Governor Tony Evers issued an executive order to postpone tomorrow's election due to COVID-19 concerns.
sentences.zh: 由于对新冠肺炎疫情的担忧，州长托尼·埃弗斯发布行政命令推迟明天的选举。

sentences.en: The bottom line is that I have an obligation to keep people safe.
sentences.zh: 最底线是我有义务保障人们的安全。

sentences.en: The governor makes his most drastic step, unilaterally postponing Tuesday's election until June, claiming that he has the emergency powers to do so.
sentences.zh: 州长采取了最激进的举措，单方面将周二的选举推迟到6月，声称他拥有这样做的紧急权力。

sentences.en: So, this is an affront to the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对共和党人来说是一种侮辱。

sentences.en: Republican legislators mounted a legal challenge immediately.
sentences.zh: 共和党议员立即发起法律挑战。

sentences.en: And they immediately initiate emergency legislation going straight to the Wisconsin Supreme Court, saying that the governor does not have the right to do this.
sentences.zh: 他们立即启动紧急立法，直接上诉至威斯康星州最高法院，称州长无权这样做。

sentences.en: And just about an hour ago, the state Supreme Court issued its ruling saying that, indeed, the election will happen tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 就在大约一个小时前，州最高法院作出裁决，称选举确实将在明天举行。

sentences.en: And the court agreed with him, ruling just hours later that the governor did not have the power to postpone the Tuesday primary, meaning the election will go on in person today.
sentences.zh: 法院支持了这一立场，在几小时后裁定州长无权推迟周二的初选，这意味着选举将于今天照常进行。

sentences.en: You know, I said I'm struck by the fact that, earlier on, you told us that Democrats and Republicans in the state,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我感到印象深刻的是，你刚才告诉我们，该州的民主党人和共和党人

sentences.en: they had basically been on the same page about this primary until the virus gets worse and the governor advocates for a different kind of voting system through absentee ballots.
sentences.zh: 在病毒恶化且州长倡导通过缺席投票采用不同的投票系统之前，他们基本在这个初选问题上意见一致。

sentences.en: And then it all breaks down, and Republicans are attempting at every turn to block him now in court.
sentences.zh: 然后一切破裂了，共和党人现在试图在各个环节通过法庭阻止他。

sentences.en: And how do you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: I mean, how do Republicans in the state legislature explain that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，州议会里的共和党人如何解释这一点？

sentences.en: Republican county chairs and folks in the state legislature say a couple things.
sentences.zh: 共和党县党部主席和州议会的人士说了几点。

sentences.en: The first is that their position hasn't changed.
sentences.zh: 首先是他们的立场没有改变。

sentences.en: They thought the governor didn't have the power then, and they don't think he has the power now to change how the election is run.
sentences.zh: 他们当时认为州长没有权力，现在也认为州长没有权力改变选举的运行方式。

sentences.en: The other point is that they see Wisconsin again as a microcosm of the conservative fight that could happen largely and what could be a new reality of how American elections are run in this pandemic era.
sentences.zh: 另一点是，他们再次将威斯康星州视为保守派斗争的一个缩影，这场斗争可能会在很大程度上发生，并可能成为这个疫情时代美国选举运行方式的新现实。

sentences.en: And in that view, dramatically expanding the electorate in these ways are not something that Republicans are all that keen on,
sentences.zh: 在这种观点下，以这些方式大幅扩大选民基础并不是共和党人十分热衷的事情，

sentences.en: because what they're worried about is an election in which people who may not have participated or may not have come out all of a sudden have the opportunity to do so and to cast a ballot.
sentences.zh: 因为他们担心的是这样一场选举：原本可能没有参与或没有出来投票的人突然有机会参与并投下一票。

sentences.en: And that kind of changes the center of power within the state.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上改变了州内的权力中心。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: If people participate in different numbers, in bigger numbers,
sentences.zh: 如果人们以不同的规模、更多的数量参与进来，

sentences.en: if it changes the type of people who want to participate in a spring election that's not necessarily always seeing the biggest turnout, that changes who can win.
sentences.zh: 如果它改变了那些想要参加并不总是投票率最高的一场春季初选的人的类型，那就会改变谁能获胜。

sentences.en: And who has benefited from those systems in the past and who might benefit if they were to change along the lines of what Governor Evers is asking for?
sentences.zh: 过去谁从这些制度中受益，如果按照埃弗斯州长要求的那样发生改变，谁又会受益？

sentences.en: It's hard to say exactly because we're talking about an unprecedented situation, but we do know that the people who are typically benefited from early voting,
sentences.zh: 很难确切地说，因为我们讨论的是一种前所未有的情况，但我们确实知道，通常从提前投票中受益的人，

sentences.en: from early registration, from online registration or vote by mail, are people who usually don't participate in the process.
sentences.zh: 从提前登记、在线登记或邮寄投票中受益的人，往往是平时不参与这一进程的人。

sentences.en: Younger voters, younger voters, younger voters, people that lean Democratic,
sentences.zh: 年轻选民，年轻选民，年轻选民，倾向于民主党的选民，

sentences.en: and just in the ways that Republicans limited early voting and that special session they had after Evers won, it's the same thought process.
sentences.zh: 正如共和党人在埃弗斯获胜后举行的特别会议上限制提前投票一样，这也是同样的思维过程。

sentences.en: That when more people get involved, that when people who typically sit out get involved, that helps Democrats.
sentences.zh: 当更多人参与进来时，当平时作壁上观的人参与进来时，这对民主党是有利的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Do Democrats acknowledge that an absentee voting system that is suddenly much more widespread than it has been in the past would be advantageous to them in Wisconsin?
sentences.zh: 民主党人是否承认，一个突然比过去普及得多的缺席投票系统对威斯康星州的他们来说是有利的？

sentences.en: They principally try to appeal to voters using small-D Democratic ideals, the general basic American principle that everyone should be given the easiest access to vote.
sentences.zh: 他们主要是试图用小写的民主理想来吸引选民，也就是每个人都应该获得最便利的投票渠道这一普遍的基本美国原则。

sentences.en: They try to appeal to people through public health measures, noting how unsafe it is for people to gather at polls.
sentences.zh: 他们试图通过公共卫生措施来吸引人们，指出人们聚集在投票站是多么不安全。

sentences.en: But when you ask folks in Democratic circles, they know that when the electorate expands, particularly in national and statewide elections, that's usually good news for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但当你问及民主党圈子里的人时，他们知道，当选民范围扩大时，特别是在全国和全州范围的选举中，对民主党来说通常是个好消息。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: This is not just a debate about how to vote in a pandemic, although clearly that's what's driving a lot of this.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一场关于如何在疫情期间投票的辩论，尽管显然这是推动其中许多事情的动力。

sentences.en: But in the background, from what you're saying, is this other question, which is whether the systems needed to vote during a pandemic may fundamentally change who votes,
sentences.zh: 但在背景中，根据你的说法，还有另一个问题，那就是在疫情期间投票所需的系统是否会从根本上改变谁去投票、

sentences.en: how many people vote, and which party wins.
sentences.zh: 多少人去投票，以及哪个党派获胜。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: This is not just about public health.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关乎公共卫生。

sentences.en: This is about access to power and the kind of most basic fundamental principles of democracy.
sentences.zh: 这关乎权力的获取以及民主的最基本原则。

sentences.en: If the system that we have been traditionally used to can't hold, what replaces it?
sentences.zh: 如果我们传统上习惯的系统无法维持，什么来取代它？

sentences.en: And we've seen real resistance to that in this state, and we may see that resistance all across the country.
sentences.zh: 我们在这个州看到了对此的真正阻力，我们可能在全国各地都会看到这种阻力。

sentences.en: Well, why would you say that?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你为什么会这么说？

sentences.en: Because it's very tempting to see this story as an anomaly, right, in that the governor of Wisconsin waited a very long time to try to postpone the state's primary,
sentences.zh: 因为人们很容易将这个故事看作是一个反常现象，对吧，威斯康星州州长花了很长时间才试图推迟该州的初选，

sentences.en: perhaps too long.
sentences.zh: 也许时间太长了。

sentences.en: And the state legislature is this hyper-partisan, conservative, activist body that is trying to use its power for political advantage.
sentences.zh: 而州议会是一个极具党派色彩的、保守的、激进的机构，正试图利用其权力谋取政治利益。

sentences.en: So all those factors would seem to make Wisconsin a bit of an outlier.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这些因素似乎使威斯康星州显得有点格格不入。

sentences.en: Well, what may seem like an anomaly right now might actually just be a pacesetter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在看起来像是个反常现象的事情，实际上可能只是一个先行者。

sentences.en: And this could be a preview as to what comes for state after state.
sentences.zh: 这可能是对一个又一个州即将发生的事情的预演。

sentences.en: If you are a place like Georgia or Louisiana or Ohio that has functionally delayed its election by three, four weeks, and if this virus persists to that time,
sentences.zh: 如果你身处佐治亚州、路易斯安那州或俄亥俄州这样实际上将选举推迟了三四个州的地方，如果这种病毒到那时依然存在，

sentences.en: there will still be questions about whether it is safe to hold in-person balloting then.
sentences.zh: 关于届时举行面对面投票是否安全的问题仍将存在。

sentences.en: And when those questions come and the remedies are proposed, whether it's online or vote by mail or the like, these same struggles of power will persiSt.
sentences.zh: 当这些问题出现并提出补救措施时，无论是线上投票、邮寄投票还是类似方式，这些相同的权力争夺仍将继续。

sentences.en: And we will see factions emerge that question whether the new systems are fair and who politically benefits from them.
sentences.zh: 我们会看到不同派别浮出水面，质疑新系统是否公平以及谁在政治上从中受益。

sentences.en: Aston, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 阿斯顿，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: On Monday night, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周一晚上，美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court sided with Republican lawmakers in Wisconsin who had opposed extending the deadline for absentee ballots in today's election.
sentences.zh: 最高法院站在了威斯康星州共和党议员的一边，这些议员曾反对延长今天选举中缺席选票的截止日期。

sentences.en: In a 5-4 ruling, the court's conservative justices wrote that such an extension, quote,
sentences.zh: 在以5比4的裁决中，该法院的保守派大法官写道，这种延长，也就是

sentences.en: fundamentally alters the nature of the election and said that all absentee ballots must be postmarked by 8 p.m.
sentences.zh: 从根本上改变了选举的性质，并表示所有缺席选票必须在

sentences.en: Tuesday night.
sentences.zh: 周二晚8点前加盖邮戳。

sentences.en: Polls in Wisconsin are scheduled to open at 7 a.m.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州的投票站计划于今天早上

sentences.en: this morning, but it's unclear how many poll workers will show up, how many polling stations will be open,
sentences.zh: 7点开放，但目前尚不清楚会有多少投票工作人员出现，会有多少投票站开放，

sentences.en: and what kinds of protections will be in place to limit the spread of the coronavirus during in-person voting.
sentences.zh: 以及将采取何种保护措施来限制冠状病毒在面对面投票期间的传播。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the virus continues to spread across Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，病毒继续在威斯康星州蔓延。

sentences.en: As of Monday, the state reported nearly 2,500 infections and 77 deaths.
sentences.zh: 截至周一，该州报告了近2500起感染病例和77起死亡病例。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: I also want to send best wishes to a very good friend of mine and a friend to our nation, Prime Minister Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我还想向我的好朋友、我们国家的朋友鲍里斯·约翰逊首相致以最美好的祝愿。

sentences.en: We're very saddened to hear that he was taken into intensive care this afternoon, a little while ago.
sentences.zh: 不久前听到他下午被送进重症监护室的消息，我们深感悲痛。

sentences.en: On Monday, British Prime Minister Boris Johnson, who tested positive for COVID-19 10 days ago,
sentences.zh: 周一，10天前新冠病毒检测呈阳性的英国首相鲍里斯·约翰逊，

sentences.en: was moved into the intensive care unit of a London hospital after his condition worsened.
sentences.zh: 在病情恶化后被转移到伦敦一家医院的重症监护室。

sentences.en: Americans are all praying for his recovery.
sentences.zh: 美国人民都在为他康复祈祷。

sentences.en: He's been a really good friend.
sentences.zh: 他一直是个非常好的朋友。

sentences.en: He's been really something very special, strong, resolute, doesn't quit, doesn't give up.
sentences.zh: 他一直是个非常特殊的人，坚强、果断、不轻言放弃、永不言败。

sentences.en: In a statement, Johnson insisted he remained in charge of the British government, but said he had deputized his foreign minister to act in his place when necessary.
sentences.zh: 在一份声明中，约翰逊坚称自己依然掌控着英国政府，但也表示在必要时他已授权外交大臣代行其职。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Iran, an epicenter of the virus in the Middle East, said it would lift a nationwide shutdown of businesses
sentences.zh: 与此同时，作为中东疫情中心的伊朗表示，将解除全国范围内的企业停工令，

sentences.en: and allow the majority of its workforce to return to work later this week.
sentences.zh: 并允许绝大多数劳动力在本周晚些时候重返工作岗位。

sentences.en: Iran's president, Hassan Rouhani, said it was important for economic activity to resume,
sentences.zh: 伊朗总统哈桑·鲁哈尼表示，恢复经济活动至关重要，

sentences.en: despite fears that it could lead to greater levels of infection.
sentences.zh: 尽管人们担心这可能会导致更高水平的感染。

sentences.en: And in the U.S., the death toll surpassed 10,000 people.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，死亡人数突破了1万人。

sentences.en: And congressional leaders began talks about a second economic relief package that House Speaker Nancy Pelosi predicted could cost more than $1 trillion.
sentences.zh: 国会领导人开始就第二轮经济纾困计划进行谈判，众议院议长南希·佩洛西预测该计划的成本可能超过1万亿美元。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运转。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》最新一期节目中，我和萨拉·凯尼格将带您了解那些试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.zh: 欢迎在各大播客平台收听。
